sourcedFrom: the R9® 9mm SOUND SUPPRESSOR SYSTEM YHM-2155-28 — UNKNOWN — no revision, edition or document number is printed in the booklet (UNKNOWN — no copyright line is printed)
cleanIntro: A sealed can, so this is maintenance rather than a teardown — the R9 body does not open and no interior disassembly is published. It direct-threads onto the barrel through a Universal Rifle Suppressor Mount coupler in its base, and that coupler is the one joint the book takes apart. Two things to know before you start: YHM's cleaning interval for this can is 2000 rounds, shorter than the 2000-3000 it prints for its rifle cans; and the caliber table in this booklet does not agree with the one in YHM's other R9 document, which the second step below covers.

steps.title: Firearm unloaded and pointed somewhere safe before the can is touched
steps.action: Clear the host and keep the muzzle in a safe direction for the whole job. YHM puts this at the head of its removal and installation section, and screwing a can on or off is exactly when a muzzle gets swung across a room.
steps.quote: Be certain the firearm is unloaded and the muzzle is pointed in a safe direction before starting this removal and installation process.
steps.cite: the R9® 9mm SOUND SUPPRESSOR SYSTEM YHM-2155-28 — UNKNOWN — no revision, edition or document number is printed in the booklet — INSTALLATION AND USE, PDF p.4 (the booklet prints no folio on any page)
steps.warn: Suppressed does not mean safe. YHM's own caution is that a suppressed firearm is just as dangerous as an unsuppressed one.

steps.title: Confirm your cartridge with YHM — the two R9 books print different caliber tables
steps.action: Do not take the caliber rating in this booklet at face value. YHM has published two R9 documents, both titled the R9 9mm and both carrying part number YHM-2155-28, and their CALIBER RATING tables do not match: this one lists a single row, 5.56mm NATO with a 16 inch minimum barrel, while the other lists four rifle rows — 7.62x51/.308, 350 Legend, 7.62x39/6.8SPC/5.56 NATO and 300 BLK. Neither table lists 9mm, on a can that is named 9mm. Ring YHM and confirm what your specific R9 is rated for before you shoot it suppressed. Nothing in this guide carries a caliber or a minimum barrel figure forward, because the source contradicts itself.
steps.prose: What both books do agree on is the consequence of getting the barrel length wrong.
steps.quote: using your suppressor on a barrel shorter than recommended can cause suppressor failure and will not be covered under warranty.
steps.cite: the R9® 9mm SOUND SUPPRESSOR SYSTEM YHM-2155-28 — UNKNOWN — no revision, edition or document number is printed in the booklet — CAUTION, under the CALIBER RATING table, PDF p.2
steps.warn: Two YHM documents, two different caliber tables, same part number. Confirm with the manufacturer, not with either table.

steps.title: This book covers the can, not your firearm
steps.action: There is no host-firearm procedure anywhere in these eight pages. YHM routes the work on the gun to a gunsmith who knows your specific model, and how to clear and strip your firearm lives in that firearm's own manual, not this one.
steps.caution: Installing it wrong voids the warranty and, in YHM's words, removes any liabilities against the manufacturer.
steps.quote: ONLY a licensed gunsmith experienced with your model of firearm should install this product.
steps.cite: the R9® 9mm SOUND SUPPRESSOR SYSTEM YHM-2155-28 — UNKNOWN — no revision, edition or document number is printed in the booklet — INSTALLATION AND USE, PDF p.4

steps.title: Let it cool before you put a hand on it
steps.action: The R9 gets hot enough to burn and hot enough to set light to what it touches. Leave it until it has cooled before removing it, and keep it away from anything meltable or flammable while it cools. This is the first line of YHM's own care section for this can, ahead of any cleaning instruction.
steps.quote: Caution! The sound suppressor can become extremely hot! Do not attempt to touch or remove the sound suppressor until it has cooled.
steps.cite: the R9® 9mm SOUND SUPPRESSOR SYSTEM YHM-2155-28 — UNKNOWN — no revision, edition or document number is printed in the booklet — R9® 9mm CARE, PDF p.3
steps.warn: Also, keep the suppressor away from anything that could melt or catch fire until it has cooled completely.

steps.title: Unscrew the can off the barrel — hand tight only, both ways
steps.action: The R9 threads straight onto the barrel through the mount in its base. Back it off anticlockwise by hand. Going on, it screws down until it is firmly secured and no barrel thread is still showing, and it is hand tightened only — YHM prints no torque figure for the can onto the barrel because there is not meant to be a wrench on it.
steps.prose: Take care starting the thread in either direction. Cross-threading a suppressor onto a barrel is how alignment gets lost.
steps.quote: place the threaded end of the R9® 9mm (1A) in line with the threads of the barrel (2a.) taking care not to cross-thread, screw the suppressor onto the barrel until it is firmly secured and no additional barrel threading is visible.
steps.cite: the R9® 9mm SOUND SUPPRESSOR SYSTEM YHM-2155-28 — UNKNOWN — no revision, edition or document number is printed in the booklet — UNIVERSAL RIFLE SUPPRESSOR MOUNT — Attach Suppressor to Firearm, PDF p.4

steps.title: Check the barrel threads match before it ever goes on
steps.action: Before the R9 is fitted to a barrel it has not been on before, check the barrel threads against YHM's published thread specification. A can screwed onto a thread it was not cut for is the second item on YHM's list of what causes baffle strikes.
steps.caution: The thread specification itself is on YHM's website, not in this booklet.
steps.quote: Before attaching your R9® 9mm Sound Suppressor you should check to ensure that the threads of the barrel meet our thread specifications.
steps.cite: the R9® 9mm SOUND SUPPRESSOR SYSTEM YHM-2155-28 — UNKNOWN — no revision, edition or document number is printed in the booklet — INSTALLATION AND USE, PDF p.4

steps.title: Wipe the outside with a cloth dipped in mild solvent
steps.action: Wipe oil, dirt and fouling off the outside of the tube using a cloth dipped in a mild gun cleaning solvent. Note this is not the damp-cloth instruction YHM gives for its rifle cans — for the R9 the book specifies a mild solvent on the cloth.
steps.quote: Excess oil, dirt, and other contaminants should be wiped from the outside surface using a cloth dipped in mild gun cleaning solvent.
steps.cite: the R9® 9mm SOUND SUPPRESSOR SYSTEM YHM-2155-28 — UNKNOWN — no revision, edition or document number is printed in the booklet — R9® 9mm CARE, PDF p.3

steps.title: Take the can off the firearm when you are done shooting
steps.action: Do not store it mounted. Condensation trapped inside is the most common problem YHM sees with suppressors, and pulling the can lets it evaporate. If it has to stay on, store the firearm muzzle-down with the action open so the inside can drain and breathe.
steps.prose: The corrosion this prevents is happening on baffles you can never reach.
steps.aside: If the sound suppressor is to remain on the firearm it is recommended that it be stored in a muzzle-down position with the action left open.
steps.quote: The most common problem encountered when using a sound suppressor is corrosion caused by condensation buildup inside the suppressor.
steps.cite: the R9® 9mm SOUND SUPPRESSOR SYSTEM YHM-2155-28 — UNKNOWN — no revision, edition or document number is printed in the booklet — R9® 9mm CARE, PDF p.3

steps.title: Nothing wet or loose goes inside the tube
steps.action: Never fire the can with water, gel, grease or anything else inside it. A suppressor with its volume filled is a pressure vessel, and YHM's stated consequence is damage to the can, damage to the host, or serious injury. It also voids the warranty outright.
steps.quote: do not use this Sound Suppressor with water or any other media inside the sound suppressor.
steps.cite: the R9® 9mm SOUND SUPPRESSOR SYSTEM YHM-2155-28 — UNKNOWN — no revision, edition or document number is printed in the booklet — WARNING!, PDF p.5
steps.warn: This booklet publishes NO solvent-soak procedure for the R9. Do not import one from YHM's rifle-can books.

steps.title: That is the whole field strip — the body does not open
steps.action: Can off the barrel, threads checked, outside wiped. No disassembly of the R9 body is published anywhere in the booklet: no baffle stack, no end cap, no core. Deep Clean covers the one joint that does come apart — the Universal Rifle Suppressor Mount coupler in the base — and the cleaning interval.
steps.prose: YHM's interval for this can is a minimum of every 2000 rounds, and it says outright that the interval moves with the ammunition, the host and the weather.
steps.quote: We recommend cleaning the sound suppressor at a minimum after every 2000 rounds.
steps.cite: the R9® 9mm SOUND SUPPRESSOR SYSTEM YHM-2155-28 — UNKNOWN — no revision, edition or document number is printed in the booklet — R9® 9mm CARE, PDF p.3

deepSteps.title: Universal Rifle Suppressor Mount coupler out of the base
deepSteps.action: The coupler screws into the bottom of the can and is the only part of the R9 that separates from the body. Hold the R9 body firmly, put a 3/4" wrench on the coupler and turn it anticlockwise to loosen it out of the base.
deepSteps.prose: This is the joint that lets the R9 change thread pitch. It is not a route into the suppressor — behind it the body is sealed.
deepSteps.quote: Hold the R9® 9mm body (1A) with a firm grip and use a 3/4” wrench (3A) in a counter-clockwise direction to loosen the coupler from the bottom of the suppressor.
deepSteps.cite: the R9® 9mm SOUND SUPPRESSOR SYSTEM YHM-2155-28 — UNKNOWN — no revision, edition or document number is printed in the booklet — Removal and Installation of Universal Rifle Suppressor Mount, PDF p.4

deepSteps.title: Coupler back in — hand-started, then the wrench
deepSteps.action: Clean the threads, then start the coupler back into the base by hand before the wrench touches it. YHM's instruction is explicitly to reverse the removal but to begin the thread by hand, because cross-threading this joint is what puts the can off-axis.
deepSteps.quote: to install, reverse these instructions, starting the thread by hand to avoid cross-threading.
deepSteps.cite: the R9® 9mm SOUND SUPPRESSOR SYSTEM YHM-2155-28 — UNKNOWN — no revision, edition or document number is printed in the booklet — Removal and Installation of Universal Rifle Suppressor Mount, PDF p.4
deepSteps.warn: YHM prints no torque figure for the coupler. Do not invent one — snug it with the 3/4" wrench and check it periodically.

deepSteps.title: Set your own interval from how you actually shoot
deepSteps.action: The 2000-round figure is a floor, not a schedule. YHM says the gap between cleanings moves with the ammunition, with what host the can is on, and with rain or humidity. A can that lives on a wet hunt gets serviced sooner than one that lives in a dry safe.
deepSteps.quote: The period between cleanings will vary depending on what type of ammunition you are shooting, the type of host firearm, and environmental conditions such as rain or high humidity.
deepSteps.cite: the R9® 9mm SOUND SUPPRESSOR SYSTEM YHM-2155-28 — UNKNOWN — no revision, edition or document number is printed in the booklet — R9® 9mm CARE, PDF p.3

deepSteps.title: Check it has not walked loose — during shooting, not just before
deepSteps.action: Firing can back the can off the barrel, and a can that has moved is a can that is no longer concentric with the bore. YHM asks the owner to check periodically that the suppressor is still firmly attached to both the firearm and the mount. Do it at magazine changes, not only at the start of the day.
deepSteps.prose: The suppressor coming loose from the host is the first item on YHM's own list of what causes baffle strikes.
deepSteps.quote: It is possible that with firing the suppressor may become loose, which can cause misalignment.
deepSteps.cite: the R9® 9mm SOUND SUPPRESSOR SYSTEM YHM-2155-28 — UNKNOWN — no revision, edition or document number is printed in the booklet — NOTE, PDF p.5
deepSteps.warn: A can that has moved does not get another magazine through it until it has been re-seated and re-checked.

cleaning.name: OUTSIDE OF THE TUBE
tasks: Wipe excess oil, dirt and other contaminants off the outside with a cloth dipped in mild gun cleaning solvent
Let the can cool completely before touching or removing it
Keep it clear of anything meltable or flammable while it cools

cleaning.name: MOUNT & THREADS
tasks: Clean the barrel threads and the threaded end of the can
Confirm the barrel threads meet YHM's published thread specification before first fitting
Check the Universal Rifle Suppressor Mount coupler is still tight in the base
Hand-start every thread — the can onto the barrel and the coupler into the base

cleaning.name: INTERVAL — 2000 ROUNDS MINIMUM
tasks: Clean at a minimum every 2000 rounds, sooner for wet or humid conditions
Never fire the can with water or any other media inside it
Do not attempt to open the body — no interior disassembly is published for the R9
No solvent-soak procedure is published for this can; do not borrow one from another YHM book

cleaning.name: STORAGE
tasks: Take the suppressor off as soon as you have finished shooting so condensation can evaporate
If it stays on, store the firearm muzzle-down with the action open

reassembly: Clean the threads, then hand-start the Universal Rifle Suppressor Mount coupler into the base of the R9 body and snug it with a 3/4" wrench.
Line the threaded end of the can up with the barrel threads and start it by hand, taking care not to cross-thread.
Screw the suppressor down until it is firmly secured and no additional barrel threading is visible.
Hand tighten only — there is no torque figure for the can onto the barrel and no wrench belongs on it.
Confirm the can is dry inside before it goes on the firearm.
fncheck: With the firearm confirmed unloaded, check the R9 is firmly seated with no barrel thread showing and no free movement, and that the mount coupler is still tight in the base. Then keep checking it as you shoot — YHM asks for a periodic check because firing can walk the can loose, and the suppressor coming loose from the host is the number one cause of baffle strikes on its own list, ahead of poor barrel threads, incorrect mount installation and poor ammunition. Separately, do not fire it suppressed until you have confirmed with YHM what your R9 is actually rated for; the two published caliber tables disagree.
